sc: Born at 30 weeks, stiff legs, scissoring, toe walking → Spastic diplegic CP
Boy climbs up his legs to stand, big calves → Gowers sign: Duchenne (CK)
OFC crossing centiles up, bulging fontanelle, sunset eyes → Hydrocephalus: cranial ultrasound
f: Higher functions · cranial nerves · tone, power, reflexes, plantars, clonus · coordination · gait · sensation · head (OFC, fontanelle), spine
UMN: ↑ tone, brisk reflexes, clonus, extensor plantar after walking age · LMN: floppy, absent reflexes, wasting, fasciculation
Polio (asymmetric) · GBS (ascending, areflexia, after diarrhoea) · transverse myelitis (sensory level)
Rickets: bossing, rosary, wide wrists, bow legs · Down: upslanting eyes, single crease, sandal gap · anaemia: pallor, koilonychia
MRI brain · CK · nerve conduction · CSF · karyotype · cranial ultrasound
Watch the child walk · compare both sides · plot the OFC
trap: An extensor plantar is normal before walking · loss of skills already gained is not CP · hand preference at 8 months = hemiplegia on the other side
